messages.subject: spatio-temporal model - group rho estimate does not change under different pc.prior choices
parts:
Hello,

I am fitting a spatiotemporal model to an invasive species' distribution on a small island ( 196 km^2) using data from ~ 160 sample stations across seven years. 

I fitted the model with a negative binomial likelihood, a few habitat fixed effects and the spde x AR1 term. Under all prior distribution choices for the AR1 term, the model returns the exact same estimate: mode = 0.967; 95% CI = 0.891 - 0.986 (down to seven significant figures). 

The priors I have used on the spatiotemporal terms are:

spde  <-  inla.spde2.pcmatern(
  mesh=mesh, alpha=2, 
  prior.range = c(0.5, 0.001), 
  prior.sigma = c(4, 0.001))


hyper_AR1 <- list(theta=list(prior='pc.cor1', param=c(0.8, 0.1))) 

(assuming the AR1 prior is vague)


I have been using the 'pc.prior' with base model = 1 so thought that this behaviour may indicate that there is not much data to support a temporal effect. However, even when I change the values to something very different (e.g. P(rho > 0.8) = 0.000001; many other values were tested) the estimate does not change. Further, if I use the 'pc.cor0' prior with the base model of no correlation the estimate is the same. 

The LCPO and WAIC scores both support including the AR1 group term vs. only replicating the spatial effect. In the replicate-only model, the spatial range estimate increases and the spatial variance estimate decreases. 

Is the data dominating the prior choices and estimating strong AR1 correlation? 

Why would the spatial range estimate increases and variance decrease in the replicate-only model? 

Any suggestions would be appreciated.

Kind regards,
Vaughn

The priors need to be seen in context. For example, what distance units is your SPDE mesh in? Metres, kilometres, or something else?
Also, if you don’t see any difference at all, perhaps you’re not actually supplying the prior information in he correct place in the code?

Finn

Hi Finn,

I am using Km units for the mesh and priors. 

Here is the relevant code for the model:

# creating adjacency matrix with stations and temporal grouping 
A.est <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh,
                          loc=as.matrix(grig.dat.spatial[,7:8]),
                          n.spde=spde$n.spde, 
                          group=grig.dat.spatial$year, 
                          n.group=n_year) 

# setting the index for the nodes
field.indices <- inla.spde.make.index(
  "nodes", 
  n.spde=spde$n.spde, 
  n.group=n_year) 


#creating the inla.stack for estimation
stack <- inla.stack(
  data=list(count = grig.dat.spatial$count), 
  A= list(A.est, 1), 
  effects=
    list(field.indices, 
         data.frame(
           Intercept=1, 
           grig.dat.spatial[,c(1,3:5,9:12)])), 
  tag="est") 



Here is the code for the mesh:
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(loc=as.matrix(grig.dat.spatial[,7:8]), boundary=domainGC,max.edge = c(0.5,20), cutoff=0.5,  
                     offset = c(1,80), min.angle = 21) 


The model formula:
formula <- count ~ -1 + Intercept +  
   moisture + urban + veg_height  + I(urban^2)  + 
  f(nodes, model=spde, group=nodes.group, control.group=list(model="ar1"), hyper = hyper_AR1)  


and the model call:
STmodel <- inla(
  formula,
  family= 'nbinomial',
  data=inla.stack.data(stack, spde=spde), 
  control.fixed =
    list(mean.intercept = 0, prec.intercept = 0.001, mean = 0, prec = 0.001), 
  control.predictor=list(
    A=inla.stack.A(stack),
    compute=TRUE, link=1), 
  control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE, waic=TRUE, config=TRUE),
  num.threads = 4, 
  verbose = TRUE, 
  control.inla = list(int.strategy='eb',strategy = "gaussian"),
  control.results=list(
    return.marginals.predictor=TRUE, 
    return.marginals.random=TRUE))

﻿Hello,

I am fitting a spatiotemporal model to an invasive species' distribution on a small island ( 196 km^2) using data from ~ 160 sample stations across seven years. 

I fitted the model with a negative binomial likelihood, a few habitat fixed effects and the spde x AR1 term. Under all prior distribution choices for the AR1 term, the model returns the exact same estimate: mode = 0.967; 95% CI = 0.891 - 0.986 (down to seven significant figures). 

The priors I have used on the spatiotemporal terms are:

spde  <-  inla.spde2.pcmatern(
  mesh=mesh, alpha=2, 
  prior.range = c(0.5, 0.001), 
  prior.sigma = c(4, 0.001))


hyper_AR1 <- list(theta=list(prior='pc.cor1', param=c(0.8, 0.1))) 

(assuming the AR1 prior is vague)


I have been using the 'pc.prior' with base model = 1 so thought that this behaviour may indicate that there is not much data to support a temporal effect. However, even when I change the values to something very different (e.g. P(rho > 0.8) = 0.000001; many other values were tested) the estimate does not change. Further, if I use the 'pc.cor0' prior with the base model of no correlation the estimate is the same. 

The LCPO and WAIC scores both support including the AR1 group term vs. only replicating the spatial effect. In the replicate-only model, the spatial range estimate increases and the spatial variance estimate decreases. 

Is the data dominating the prior choices and estimating strong AR1 correlation? 

Why would the spatial range estimate increases and variance decrease in the replicate-only model? 

Any suggestions would be appreciated.

Kind regards,
Vaughn

On 16 Sep 2020, at 17:12, vaughn...@gmail.com <vaughn...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿Hello,

I am fitting a spatiotemporal model to an invasive species' distribution on a small island ( 196 km^2) using data from ~ 160 sample stations across seven years. 

I fitted the model with a negative binomial likelihood, a few habitat fixed effects and the spde x AR1 term. Under all prior distribution choices for the AR1 term, the model returns the exact same estimate: mode = 0.967; 95% CI = 0.891 - 0.986 (down to seven significant figures). 

The priors I have used on the spatiotemporal terms are:

spde  <-  inla.spde2.pcmatern(
  mesh=mesh, alpha=2, 
  prior.range = c(0.5, 0.001), 
  prior.sigma = c(4, 0.001))


hyper_AR1 <- list(theta=list(prior='pc.cor1', param=c(0.8, 0.1))) 

(assuming the AR1 prior is vague)


I have been using the 'pc.prior' with base model = 1 so thought that this behaviour may indicate that there is not much data to support a temporal effect. However, even when I change the values to something very different (e.g. P(rho > 0.8) = 0.000001; many other values were tested) the estimate does not change. Further, if I use the 'pc.cor0' prior with the base model of no correlation the estimate is the same. 

The LCPO and WAIC scores both support including the AR1 group term vs. only replicating the spatial effect. In the replicate-only model, the spatial range estimate increases and the spatial variance estimate decreases. 

Is the data dominating the prior choices and estimating strong AR1 correlation? 

Why would the spatial range estimate increases and variance decrease in the replicate-only model? 

Any suggestions would be appreciated.

Kind regards,
Vaughn

On 16 Sep 2020, at 17:12, vaughn...@gmail.com <vaughn...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿Hello,

I am fitting a spatiotemporal model to an invasive species' distribution on a small island ( 196 km^2) using data from ~ 160 sample stations across seven years. 

I fitted the model with a negative binomial likelihood, a few habitat fixed effects and the spde x AR1 term. Under all prior distribution choices for the AR1 term, the model returns the exact same estimate: mode = 0.967; 95% CI = 0.891 - 0.986 (down to seven significant figures). 

The priors I have used on the spatiotemporal terms are:

spde  <-  inla.spde2.pcmatern(
  mesh=mesh, alpha=2, 
  prior.range = c(0.5, 0.001), 
  prior.sigma = c(4, 0.001))


hyper_AR1 <- list(theta=list(prior='pc.cor1', param=c(0.8, 0.1))) 

(assuming the AR1 prior is vague)


I have been using the 'pc.prior' with base model = 1 so thought that this behaviour may indicate that there is not much data to support a temporal effect. However, even when I change the values to something very different (e.g. P(rho > 0.8) = 0.000001; many other values were tested) the estimate does not change. Further, if I use the 'pc.cor0' prior with the base model of no correlation the estimate is the same. 

The LCPO and WAIC scores both support including the AR1 group term vs. only replicating the spatial effect. In the replicate-only model, the spatial range estimate increases and the spatial variance estimate decreases. 

Is the data dominating the prior choices and estimating strong AR1 correlation? 

Why would the spatial range estimate increases and variance decrease in the replicate-only model? 

Any suggestions would be appreciated.

Kind regards,
Vaughn

parts: Ah - I have found the simple mistake... When specifying the prior in the model formula I did not put the group prior in the control.group list; I had it outside of the control.group argument.
f(nodes, model=spde, group=nodes.group, control.group=list(model="ar1"), hyper = hyper_AR1)

vs.  
 f(nodes, model=spde, group=nodes.group, control.group=list(model="ar1", hyper = hyper_AR1)) 

Now the estimates change with my prior choices, albeit only slight changes.
